text.tspan: MIX PROTOCOL API CHANGES / CONNECTIONS AND MESSAGES
Legacy reply-expecting connections handle one request. MixTransport manages sessions and streams.
with a reference to this connection’s
ExitLayer takes it after the handler returns.
At B: ExitLayer sends the response
Reply returns through Mix; A recovers it.
If the destination is beyond the exit, the exit uses a regular libp2p connection instead of MixExitConnection.
The exit collects that reply using the codec’s response reader.
createSurb returns a SURB and its credential; send and sendWithSurb send individual messages.
The caller owns credential storage and dispatch. The legacy connection API remains available.
Connection objects are local wrappers, not an end-to-end physical connection.
In both modes, replies return via SURBs. At A, recovered bytes enter the requesting connection’s incoming queue.

g.text: 02 — A service receives the complete message payload
MIX PROTOCOL API CHANGES · FORWARD DELIVERY
A service receives the complete message payload
Forward sending and receiving no longer require a connection-style request/reply exchange.
Example: one Mix message before padding
The service owns the payload format. Mix selects the callback; MixTransport decodes the frame.
03 — One SURB, one credential, two different owners
MIX PROTOCOL API CHANGES · RETURN CAPACITY
One SURB, one credential, two different owners
createSurb(destination) returns a pair; it does not send a packet or register a legacy credential.
First hop + Sphinx header + reply key
B can construct one return message.
The SURB contains a reply key, but not the initiator’s return-path secrets.
04 — Describe the destination without adding it to the relay pool
MIX PROTOCOL API CHANGES · DESTINATION AND ROUTE
Describe the destination without adding it to the relay pool
The MixPubInfo send overload supplies the final hop; intermediate hops still come from the pool.
Mix public key + libp2p public key
No temporary pool insertion or peer-store address rewriting.
Peer-ID-only send remains available: Mix resolves B from the node pool.
“Explicit destination” still means delivery through Mix relays, not a direct network connection.
05 — Return sending and recovery become explicit operations
MIX PROTOCOL API CHANGES · REVERSE DELIVERY
Return sending and recovery become explicit operations
The API returns raw reply information before the caller selects its credential.
Empty service; one SURB per call
A SURB is spent once send is invoked,
even if the send returns an error.
One raw-reply callback slot per Mix instance.
The caller manages credential lifetime. recoverReply performs cryptography, not store consumption.
06 — New and legacy consumers share the packet-processing path
New and legacy consumers share the packet-processing path
A local dispatch decision selects the owner; it does not acknowledge a remote message.
New message send uses exit = destination.
Handled: recover, process or discard here
Recovered bytes enter the connection queue.
